sections.history: Tiruthelicheri, now the locality of Koilpatthu on the edge of Karaikal town, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the lower Kaveri country, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. Though Karaikal lies in the Union Territory of Puducherry, the shrine belongs wholly to the Tamil Shaiva sacred geography of the delta. The sthala tradition holds the place to be of immense antiquity, named Brahmavanam in the Satya yuga, Sameevanam in the Treta, Anandavanam in the Dwapara and Muktivanam in the Kali yuga. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian temple of modest size, the shrine enshrines Parvatheeswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Parvathi Ammai — also called Sakthi Nayaki and Swayamvara Tapasvini — in her own shrine, a Nandi, and the parivara devatas. The temple is oriented so that at a fixed season the sun's rays reach the lingam, the mark of a Bhaskara Kshetram, a place blessed by the sun-god's own worship.
sections.legends: The goddess Parvati is said to have performed long and ardent penance here, worshipping Shiva, until the lord drew her into himself as a part of his own form — from which she is praised as Swayamvara Tapasvini, 'she who won him by penance,' and the lord as Parvatheeswarar. A second legend tells that Surya, the sun-god, came here to worship Shiva and dug the temple tank; pleased, Shiva restored the sun's full brightness, and so the place became a Bhaskara Kshetram. For ten days from Panguni 13 (March–April) the sun's rays fall upon the lingam in the evenings.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Suryapuja days of Panguni, when the sun's rays touch the lingam, as its special observance, along with Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri and the Mondays of Karthikai. Devotees come for the grace of the sun-blessed lord and the penance-won goddess.
sections.experience: At Koilpatthu the pilgrim comes to a shrine of deep antiquity where penance and sunlight meet. Before Parvatheeswarar and Parvathi Ammai, the visitor remembers the goddess who won the lord by her austerity and the sun who regained his brightness here — and, in the Panguni days, may see the evening light reach the lingam, the living sign of a Bhaskara Kshetram.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: The temple is at Koilpatthu, about 3 km from the Karaikal bus stand (Tiruthelicheri/Koilpatthu, PIN 609602, Puducherry UT). Karaikal has its own railway station and bus services; local autos and taxis reach Koilpatthu.
